segments.text: [laughs] I usually start my day with coffee. It's become a little ritual for me. Sometimes I brew it at home, grind the beans, listen to the sound of the machine, wait for that smell to fill the kitchen.

Other times, I just stop by a café and grab one on my way to work. Either way, that first sip, it feels like the real beginning of the day. It's funny, isn't it? Coffee isn't just coffee. It's a pause, a moment to breathe, to wake up not only my body, but also my mind. I think it's less about caffeine and more about how it makes me feel. Warm mug in my hands, a quiet moment before the world gets noisy. Almost like saying, "Okay, I'm here. Let's start the day." Of course, not every morning is perfect. Sometimes I spill it. Sometimes I rush out the door and grab a quick cup, barely tasting it. But even then, it still feels like a small ritual that grounds me. And coffee means different things to different people. For some, it's comfort. For others, it's fuel. Some people need two or three cups before they can even say a word. Others enjoy just one slowly, like a treat. Personally, I like to notice the details, the smell, the first sip, the way it warms me up from the inside. It's a reminder that even in a busy morning, I can choose a small ritual that makes me feel good.

Maybe for you it isn't coffee. Maybe it's tea. Maybe it's juice or water or nothing at all. But we all have little habits that shape the start of our day. And those habits, they matter more than we think. They set the tone.
